items.what: harness.planner (tests/harness.lua:2632-2642) reads the TOC file list with its own line parser beside harness.load's (tests/harness.lua:2410-2413), the canonical one; tests/locales_spec.lua:65 is a third reader
items.why: Both turn TOC lines into load paths in client order. harness.load strips a trailing carriage return and skips blank and # lines, and names the file through ADDON; harness.planner does neither and retypes the file name. The differences look like accidental drift: with a CRLF TOC the planner copy matches no path and silently loads nothing, and a blank or comment line between Planning\Model.lua and Planning\Order.lua would make it call loadfile on that line, while harness.load keeps working. Neither case occurs with the TOC as it is now (LF, no gaps in that range), so no behaviour differs yet; a change to how TOC lines are read must be made in both. A single local iterator over the TOC's file paths would serve both.
items.reason: tests/harness.lua: harness.planner, harness.load and tests/locales_spec.lua:65 each parse the TOC file list; only the planner copy lacks the blank and # skip, so a comment line between two Planning entries fails its loadfile. Give all three one TOC reader? It changes what the planner copy accepts.

items.what: tests/laps_spec.lua:63-79 duplicates tests/playthrough_spec.lua:69-85 and its placement index; make one shared test-side validator in tests/harness.lua the canonical home.
items.why: Both validators are byte-identical and enforce the same data-placement contract: a direct indexed point, or an indexed ring centre plus an indexed shape containing the step according to Model.Yards. Their Key/Add helpers and index construction also encode the same four-decimal keys, quest start/finish places, objective map fallback and NPC places (laps:32-59; playthrough:47-65). Laps additionally collects random-character givers and exclusive groups in its quest loop; that is intentional fixture setup and can stay separate. Their callers differ only in how they generate routes (laps Walk at line 150 versus playthrough at line 238), not in what makes a point valid. A correction to rounding, objective placement or area-entry validation must therefore land in both copies. Whole-repository searches found no third Placed implementation or equivalent harness helper. Extract the existing playthrough validator/index into shared test support and have both suites call it, keeping it independent of production placement logic.

items.quote: check(builtFrames >= 1, label .. ": the build was not sliced")
items.what: The check named for slicing cannot fail when slicing is removed: builtFrames is already 1 after the first frame of any queued rebuild, because ns.Rebuilding() is just pendingRebuild, which ns.Invalidate sets before the loop starts.
items.why: Proved on a scratch copy: with the coroutine.yield() in Planning/Journeys.lua YieldCards replaced by a no-op, `luajit -joff tests/plan_bench.lua` still exits 0 (worst rebuild 3.164 ms, only the local AGF_BENCH_STRICT budget would notice). The check only fails if no rebuild was queued at all. Slicing itself stays covered by tests/rebuild_slice_spec.lua, which fails on the same scratch copy (assert at line 24). Either assert builtFrames > 1 for a profile known to slice, or reword the message to what it guards (a rebuild ran in the sampled frames).
items.reason: tests/plan_bench.lua:284 'the build was not sliced' checks builtFrames >= 1, which only proves a rebuild was queued (ns.Rebuilding() is pendingRebuild); with the yield in Planning/Journeys.lua removed the bench still exits 0. Require more than one build frame, or reword the message and leave slicing to tests/rebuild_slice_spec.lua?

items.quote: -- F2: at most MAX_JOURNEYS journeys, each with at least one step the player can take now. The standing rules hold on
items.what: Comment names a MAX_JOURNEYS cap that no longer exists and that nothing below asserts (also on line 264); reword both to what the block checks.
items.why: rg MAX_JOURNEYS over the repository matches only these two comment lines: no constant in Planning/Model.lua or types/Namespace.lua. The block asserts unique keys and 1..MAX_STEPS steps, never a card count, and tests/model_spec.lua asserts more than six cards ('level 19: all useful destinations remain accessible'), matching docs/design.md 2.2 'Offer every eligible journey'.

items.quote:
for _, other in ipairs(route.journeys) do
				equal(other == journey or other.key ~= journey.key, true, label .. ": another zone than the story's")
			end
items.what: The loop only asserts that no other card shares this card's key, which the 'no duplicate journey' check a few lines above already proves for every card; it never compares against the story's zone as labelled, so remove it or compare the map with the story card's.
items.why: Lines 75-79 fail on any repeated card.key before this loop runs, so `other.key ~= journey.key` for other ~= journey is always true here. A next-zone card for the story's own zone would have the same key 'zone:<map>' and is caught by that earlier check; tests/model_spec.lua ('never the story's own zone', 'in Here, There is next') covers the rule on fixtures.

-- The next-zone rule: another zone than the story's, one the player hasn't outgrown, with at least 3 quests
		-- they can take now.
items.what: Comment states a three-quest threshold the assertion below it does not hold (`quests >= 1`); update the comment to the rule the code checks.
items.why: Line 107 asserts `quests >= 1` with label 'useful quests available now'; tests/model_spec.lua pins 'two open now are a useful option' and Planning/Model.lua:3753 says 'Every zone with a useful pickup is an option', so the threshold in the comment is a leftover of an older rule.

items.quote:
local previous = h.ns.Route()
		assert(h.ns.Route() == previous, "a partial build is not visible: the route is unchanged mid-flight")
items.what: The mid-flight atomicity assert compares two consecutive ns.Route() calls, so it cannot fail; capture `previous` before h.ns.Invalidate() so the assert compares the mid-flight route with the pre-build one.
items.why: `previous` is taken after the first slice, then Route() is read again on the next line. Core/Core.lua ns.Route (line 717) returns cachedRoute; even if the `not rebuildCo` guard were removed and Route() rebuilt synchronously mid-flight, the first call would do it and the second would return the same table, so the assert still passes. A scratch probe capturing the route before Invalidate() showed mid == before is true and after-flush ~= before is true, so the corrected assert passes today and would catch a visible partial build. The later `Route() ~= previous` only proves the commit happened.

items.what: The test names carry a code review's finding IDs (B1, A1, A2, A3, A3b, A4, B2, B3, B4, B5, B8, B9) and the file is named after that review; drop the ID prefixes and move each case to its feature's spec (session, order, tracker, pvp, sound) or name the file for its subject.

items.what: The 'click the visible TabSystemTopButtonTemplate tab with this label' loop is written three times (scenes.lua:291-299, 309-317, 351-359); make one local helper (label in, clicks out) beside Window() and call it from all three.
items.why: jscpd evidence clone tests/scenes.lua [350:46 - 360:19]; read all three: the Find predicate (IsVisible, stockTemplate == 'TabSystemTopButtonTemplate', GetText() == label) and the h.Click loop are identical, and only the label differs (the first is already parameterised over prep/bosses/loot). items.reason: The lens excludes small idioms: these copies are a Find-and-Click loop using the canonical tests/harness.lua helpers, differing only in the label expression and surrounding scene. Searching origin/cb/route-stop-api shows the same shape; the proposed extraction touches no hot file.

tf = { spells = { SPELL, SPELL, SPELL } },

items.what: The 'both asides' options `tf = { spells = { SPELL, SPELL, SPELL } }, talents = 1` are restated inline five times (scenes.lua:127-128, 228-229, 243-244, 262-263, 303-304) before the ASIDES table that names them is defined at line 362; define ASIDES beside SPELL and build each Load's extras from it.

items.quote: objectives = { { type = "item", numFulfilled = 0, numRequired = 1, finished = false, text = "Necklace" } },
items.what: fully dead: the keys numFulfilled, numRequired and finished on a snapshot log objective; nothing reads them, the planner reads have, need and done
items.why: input.log is the snapshot log (AGFLogObjective in types/Namespace.lua: type, text, done, have, need), built by Core/State.lua Objectives() from the client's info.numFulfilled/numRequired/finished. The only readers of those three names are Core/State.lua (on the client's info table) and tests/harness.lua:1413 (building that client table); Planning/Steps.lua OpenSlots and Objective read objective.type, done, have, need, text. So this entry reaches the planner with have, need and done nil and the three keys unread. tests/fixtures/characters.lua uses the have/need/done shape. No string-built key, registry or persisted name involved; checked dynamic access (no objective[key] lookups in Planning), data-driven lookup and the harness. The spec's assertions (step counts, visit identity) pass either way.

items.what: BUG: the smoke spec's "load" and "final" checks run an empty action through Run, which only reports errors added while the action runs, so they can never fail and errors raised during harness.load are never seen; replace them with a direct assertion that #h.errors == 0 after load (and drop the no-op finals).
items.why: Run (lines 24-38) takes before = #h.errors and fails only if #h.errors > before after fn; with `function() end` nothing can change. Lines 498, 520 and 541 are such no-ops, and the comment at 519 claims 'the profile left no error behind'. Proved with a scratch probe: harness.load with a setup that schedules a throwing C_Timer.After(0) callback returns with #h.errors == 1, and the Run-style comparison stays false, as does every later Run because each re-reads `before`. No other line of smoke_spec reads h.errors, so a load-time error in any of the 25 profile runs passes; other specs (window_spec `clean(h, "load")`) cover only their own profiles.
items.guard: lens-only: fixed with a spec check that fails without it

items.what: Checks gated on environment variables nothing in the repository sets: the `if nativeRoot then` setup and its five checks (native GetBlock, Block.Free, animation), and the companion-join loop over AGF_TRACKER_HOSTS, never run in the gate or CI.
items.why: No reference to TRACKER_UI_ROOT, AGF_TRACKER_HOSTS (or TRACKER_HOST_SOURCE in tests/tracker_geometry_spec.lua) in scripts, CI, docs or config, so these paths are unexercised here and can rot. They may be driven from outside the repository (a sibling addon or a client source checkout), which this audit could not see; the shared-host behaviour itself is still checked by `addons share a single private host`.
items.reason: The premise is false for the quoted line: .github/workflows/ci.yml:22-25 (step 'Native tracker integration') runs tools/fetch_tracker_ui.py and then `TRACKER_UI_ROOT=tools/.cache/tracker-ui luajit tests/tracker_host_spec.lua`, so the nativeRoot setup and its five checks run in CI on main and on all four in-flight refs. AGF_TRACKER_HOSTS has no setter in this repository but is a cross-repository seam: an out-of-tree driver (wow-handoff/test-tracker-load-orders.py:32) sets it to load sibling addons' host files in each order, and the sibling legacy-forever spec reads the same variable.

items.what: The frame stub defines GetBottom twice: tests/tracker_host_spec.lua:33-35 (f:GetBottom) and tests/tracker_host_spec.lua:51-53 (f.GetBottom). The second assignment replaces the first on every stub frame; the canonical copy is the later one at 51-53, the earlier one at 33-35 is the leftover.
items.why: Both are assigned to the same key of the same table inside frame(), so the first never runs. They differ: the first ignores a set self.bottom and guards GetTop with 'or 0' (GetTop always returns a number, self.top or 640); the second returns self.bottom when set, which the spec relies on (minimap.bottom, host.bottom at lines 101, 448, 449). The difference is accidental drift from an earlier version, and an edit to the first copy would silently have no effect.

items.what: fully dead: the frame stub's first GetBottom (lines 33-35) is overwritten by the second definition at lines 51-53 before any frame is returned; delete the first.
items.why: Both are assigned to the same key `f.GetBottom` inside `frame()`; the later `function f.GetBottom(self) return self.bottom or self:GetTop() - self:GetHeight() end` always wins. No dynamic dispatch, manifest or external caller can reach an overwritten closure. The spec's 0 luacheck warnings do not cover a field reassigned on a table.
